title: The Gotcha Day Expedition
clue: A day that is yours, marked with three little stops.
reveal: Gotcha day, adoption day, home day: use whichever name and date feel right, even a rough guess. Today is a three-stop expedition built from your dog's favorites, one tiny new thing and a cozy return home.
objective: Visit your dog's favorite spot, offer one gentle new experience and come home to a cozy celebration.
instructions: Pick the day and the name you like, or simply choose a day. You do not need the exact date or any story about the past; many dogs arrive with an unknown history and that is fine.
Pack a favorite toy, a clean cloth from their bed and one new-to-them item that is plain and safe, such as a different towel or textured mat. Avoid candles, balloons, ribbon, bows and party foods.
Stop one, the Favorite: go to the spot or route your dog loves most, outdoors or a favorite room, and enjoy it for ten minutes at their pace.

Stop two, the New Thing: offer one small first, such as turning down a street you have not tried or laying the new mat for them to investigate. Let them approach or skip it. Move on calmly if they are unsure.
Stop three, Home: settle at home. Spread the new towel beside their bed, sit nearby and let them rest. Read aloud a short note about what you like about them today.
Keep the note somewhere you can add to next year.
twist: The day is built from the dog's present favorites and one tiny first, never from the past, so it works for any history.
variations: Home-only: do all three stops in your living space.
Puppy or newly arrived dog: stay at home and pick two stops. Puppies stay home until your vet says public places are fine.
Senior dog: shorten Stop one to a comfortable bench or a sunny rug.
Reward the stops with extra time with their favorite toy or a slow sniff walk; no food needed.
completion: You have visited the favorite and the new, settled at home and read the note.
photoIdea: Your dog relaxed on the new mat or at their favorite spot, taken naturally, kept on your phone.
memoryPrompt: What was the favorite stop, and what would you add next year?
safety: Keep candles, balloons, ribbon and party foods away; they are swallowing and burning hazards.
Offer the new item and stay close; let your dog walk away from it.
Leash on outdoors; check pavement and weather. Puppies stay home until your vet says public places are fine.
